response.body:
## Survey: OpenCode (step 1) Tested against OpenCode **1.19.4** (npm `opencode-ai`, the current `latest`), installed into a scratch prefix with a throwaway HOME and XDG dirs. Source read at the matching tag, [`sst/opencode@v1.19.4`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/tree/v1.19.4). No repo changes. ### Recommendation on separation Most of the separation isn't needed, because OpenCode already reads the two formats this repo is built from: - **Skills:** OpenCode loads `SKILL.md` natively, from `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `.opencode/skills/`, and any directory listed in `skills.paths` (scanned for `**/SKILL.md`). Unknown frontmatter such as `allowed-tools` is ignored. Pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `plugins/` found all five skills with no change. ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/), [source](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/skill/index.ts)) - **Commands:** OpenCode's command format is the same markdown-with-frontmatter, with the same `$ARGUMENTS`. It does **not** read `.claude/commands/` or a plugin's `commands/` (only `.opencode/command(s)/`, `~/.config/opencode/command(s)/` and the `command` config key; I checked: a file in `.claude/commands/` doesn't show up). The only thing in our command files OpenCode can't use as-is is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/), [source](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/config/command.ts)) - **Claude Code plugins themselves** (`.claude-plugin/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, marketplaces, the plugin cache under `~/.claude/plugins/`) are not read at all. The `~/.claude` skill scan is anchored at `~/.claude/skills/`, so skills installed as Claude Code plugins are invisible to OpenCode. The piece that makes one tree serve both: an OpenCode server plugin's `config` hook gets the live merged config and can add to it. I prototyped a 50-line plugin (plain JS, no dependencies) that, for each `plugins/

/`, appends `plugins/

/skills` to `skills.paths`, turns each `plugins/

/commands/*.md` into an OpenCode command with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by the real path, and replaces `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` in a loaded skill's text through `tool.execute.after` on the `skill` tool. Installed by OpenCode from a git URL (`"plugin": [["name@git+file:///…", {"plugins": ["forge-tracker"]}]]`), it registered `forge-tracker` and `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom` with the script paths resolved into OpenCode's package cache, and the script ran from there with its executable bit intact. So the layout I'd propose leaves the Claude Code layout where it is and adds OpenCode code only where there's no shared form: ``` package.json # "main": "harness/opencode/index.js"; makes the repo an OpenCode plugin harness/opencode/index.js # the one OpenCode entry: registers skills + commands, resolves the two variables, # adds per-plugin extras; plugin options pick which plugins to enable plugins/

/ .claude-plugin/plugin.json # Claude Code only (unchanged) skills/

/SKILL.md, scripts/ # shared; keep ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} commands/*.md # shared; Claude Code reads them natively, the OpenCode entry registers them hooks/ # Claude Code only (hooks.json, function-hooks modules) harness/opencode/*.ts|js # only where a plugin needs OpenCode code (session-decisions; worktree-tidy's # session-start note); index.js imports these ``` Moving the Claude Code parts under `harness/claude-code/` buys nothing: Claude Code expects `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` at the plugin root and finds `commands/`, `skills/` and `hooks/` there by default, and the skills and commands are the shared format anyway. The one plugin where a real core/binding split pays off is session-decisions (below). Why one package at the repo root rather than one per plugin: OpenCode installs plugins through npm specifiers, and a git specifier can't point at a subdirectory, so `git+https://github.com/lokkju/skills.git` only works with a `package.json` at the root. Per-plugin packages would mean publishing each to npm. [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) ships exactly this shape for its many harnesses: a shared `skills/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `.codex-plugin/` and so on beside it, and a root `package.json` whose `main` is `.opencode/plugins/superpowers.js`, installed with `"plugin": ["superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git"]` ([INSTALL](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md), [plugin](https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/main/.opencode/plugins/superpowers.js)). Its plugin registers skills through the same `config` hook. Skills-only installs keep working without the OpenCode entry: `npx skills add lokkju/skills -a opencode` (vercel-labs `skills` 1.7.4) copies the skills into `.agents/skills/`, which OpenCode reads. Tested from a local checkout. Without the entry, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` isn't filled in; OpenCode appends `Base directory for this skill:

` to the loaded skill, and our SKILL.md text already tells the model to put that directory in its place. A model that copies the command verbatim gets `/scripts/term-record: No such file or directory` (tested), so the entry's substitution is worth having. A moving target to know about: OpenCode has a **V2 plugin API** in its source tree (`define({ id, setup })`, `ctx.skill.transform`, `ctx.command.transform`; [README](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/v2/promise/README.md)), and superpowers' install notes say V2 hosts (2.0.4+) use a `plugins` key and reject a bare file path. The released npm package is still 1.19.4 with the V1 API, which is what I tested. superpowers' plugin handles both from one file; ours could do the same later. ### Per plugin | Plugin | Works in OpenCode unchanged | Needs an OpenCode equivalent | Can't port | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | forge-release | Skill and `github-app-create` (discovered; script runs from a skills-folder copy). | Nothing: no commands or hooks. | None. | | forge-tracker | Skill and `forge-tracker` script. | `/catchup`, `/next`, `/groom`: registered from the same `commands/*.md` by the OpenCode entry with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolved (tested). `argument-hint` has no OpenCode field and is dropped. | None. | | term-recorder | Skill and `term-record`; tested end to end (skill loaded through OpenCode's `skill` tool, script run through `bash`). It also drives OpenCode's own TUI: I used it to snap OpenCode for this survey. | `allowed-tools`: OpenCode ignores it. Its default permission is `"*": "allow"` and skill directories are pre-allowed for `external_directory`, so it only matters for a user who sets `bash` to `ask`/`deny`. For them, the entry's `config` hook can add `"/scripts/term-record *": "allow"` (tested: the script ran while `echo` was denied by the project's `bash: {"*": "deny"}`). The rule is session-wide, not scoped to the skill being loaded. The "Claude Code as the target" section is Claude-specific; an OpenCode-target section would be new text. | None. | | worktree-tidy | Skill and `worktree-tidy report`. | The `SessionStart` note: a server plugin can run `worktree-tidy hook` on the `session.created` event and inject the note through `experimental.chat.system.transform`, or show it as a toast. Hooks exist in 1.19.4 (both are triggered in source); not tested. `allowed-tools` as for term-recorder. | None. | | session-decisions | The skill and its labelled-list fallback (#114). | Everything the mod does, written against OpenCode's APIs. `decision_*` tools: a plugin's `tool` map (custom tools tested). TaskCreate labelling: OpenCode's task list is `todowrite`, which replaces the whole list; `tool.execute.before` sees and can rewrite its args (seen, rewrite not tested). Hand-off check: the `session.idle` event fires at turn end (seen) and `experimental.text.complete` exposes the final text. Sidebar, footer, toasts, Accept: OpenCode has a TUI plugin API (`tui.json` `plugin`, a module `{ id, tui }`) with `api.slots.register` for `sidebar_content`, `session_prompt_right`, `app_bottom` and others, `api.ui.toast`, `DialogSelect`, `Prompt`, routes and keymap commands ([types](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/tui.ts)); OpenCode's own sidebar Todo list is built on it ([todo.tsx](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/sidebar/todo.tsx)). I loaded a TUI plugin and its toast showed; a sidebar section wasn't tested (it needs Solid/OpenTUI JSX). The TUI API isn't on the public plugins page. | Transcript rows (`● queued D3`, `✓ D3 · …`): there is no per-tool rendering slot. No TUI at all under `opencode run`, `serve`, ACP, web or desktop, so there the fallback list is the answer. | | session-history | The skills load. | claude-session-index reads Claude Code JSONL transcripts; OpenCode keeps sessions in SQLite (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) and has `opencode session` and `opencode export ` for JSON. Support means a new reader in [claude-session-index](https://github.com/lokkju/claude-session-index), not work in this repo. | Nothing, but nothing is useful until that reader exists. | For session-decisions my recommendation is: the fallback list is the OpenCode story now, and a second step is a server plugin with the `decision_*` tools, a store, and an idle-time hand-off toast, which works headless (and so for the cattle runner in lokkju/infra#214). The sidebar is a third step if wanted. The pure modules (`queue.ts`, `subject.ts`, `handoff.ts`, `reconcile.ts`, `lineage.ts`, `forge.ts`, `markdown.ts`, `more.ts`, about 1,300 lines) import nothing but each other and `types`, so they can move to a shared `core/` used by both `register.tsx` (Claude Code, 1,347 lines) and an OpenCode binding. That's the one plugin where a per-harness split inside the plugin is real work rather than a convention. ### Tested vs read Tested on OpenCode 1.19.4, with a scripted OpenAI-compatible mock standing in for the model (no credentials used), via `opencode debug skill`, `opencode serve` (`GET /skill`, `GET /command`), `opencode run --format json`, and the TUI under term-recorder: - `skills.paths` pointed at `plugins/` lists all five skills; `.agents/skills/` (from `npx skills add … -a opencode --copy`) and a symlink in `.claude/skills/` are found without config. - All four scripts run from a skills-folder copy (`--help`). - End to end: `skill` tool loads term-recorder, OpenCode prints the base directory, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` in a bash command expands to empty and fails, the plugin substitution fixes the text, the resolved script runs. - `.opencode/commands/*.md` is listed and shows in the `/` menu; `.claude/commands/*.md` is not. - A plugin's `config` hook adds commands, `skills.paths` entries and `permission.bash` rules, and all three take effect. - A plugin's custom tool is callable; `tool.execute.before`/`after`, `chat.message` and the `event` hook (including `session.idle`) fire. - Install from a git URL with plugin options, as described above. - A TUI plugin loads from `tui.json` and shows a toast. Read only, not tested: the TUI sidebar slots, injecting a session-start note, rewriting `todowrite` args, the V2 plugin API, and whether a plugin's `permission.ask` hook works: it's typed in [`Hooks`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/plugin/src/index.ts) but nothing in 1.19.4's server triggers it, so pre-approval has to go through the `config` hook. I didn't run a real model, didn't install the `git+https` form of this repo (it has no `package.json` yet), and didn't install superpowers (third-party code). Other sources: [plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), [config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/), [rules](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/) (AGENTS.md first, CLAUDE.md fallback; `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE*`), [permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [`tool/skill.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts), [`plugin/index.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts), [`agent/agent.ts`](https://github.com/sst/opencode/blob/v1.19.4/packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts) (default permissions), [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills). For step 4 (CI): the cheap smoke test needs no model. `npx skills add -a opencode -y --copy` into a temp project, run each script's `--help` from there, and assert `opencode debug skill` lists them. The mock-model run is a slightly bigger test that also proves the variable substitution and command registration. ### Open questions 1. One OpenCode package at the repo root, with plugin options to pick plugins (what I'd do, and what git install allows), or per-plugin packages published to npm? 2. Target only the V1 plugin API that ships today, or V1 and V2 from one file the way superpowers does? 3. Should the OpenCode entry add `bash` allow rules for the skills' scripts? They're session-wide, unlike `allowed-tools`, and only matter when a user has tightened `bash`. 4. session-decisions in OpenCode: fallback list only, tools plus hand-off toast, or the full sidebar? 5. Distribution and versions: install from `git+https` (pins by ref), or publish to npm, and if so whether yeet should version the OpenCode package as its own target.

In the session-decisions panel, a DECIDE item with a recommendation gets an **Accept** button, which answers `D<k>: go with <recommendation>`, and it counts toward **Accept all**. An ACTION item gets only **Done**, even when its subject carries a recommendation.

In practice many ACTION items are approvals the agent can carry out once the user says go, and they come with a recommendation:

```
A12 ACTION: approve merging owner/repo#34 (CI green) (recommend merge) [owner/repo#34]
A13 ACTION: approve merging owner/repo#56 and tagging v1.2.0 (recommend merge and tag) [owner/repo#56]
```

For these, **Done** is the wrong word: the user hasn't done anything. They want to approve the step so the agent does it. Today they have to type `A12: go` by hand.

## Proposal

- When an ACTION item's body has a `(recommend ...)` clause, show an **Accept** button beside **Done**. It answers `A<k>: go with <recommendation>`, matching the DECIDE wording, so the agent gets the same signal either way.
- Include those ACTION items in **Accept all** (in `register.tsx`, the `accepts` list now reads the recommendation only for `item.kind === 'DECIDE'`).
- Show the `recommends <choice>` chip on ACTION items that have one, as DECIDE items do.
- Keep **Done** for ACTION items, recommendation or not, for the case where the user really did the step themselves.
- An ACTION item without a recommendation keeps only **Done**.

## Notes

- `recommendation()` and `shortRecommendation()` in `hooks/subject.ts` already parse the clause; the change is which kinds the panel applies them to.
- The skill text (SKILL.md) can say ACTION items that need the user's approval should carry a `(recommend ...)` clause, so they get the button.
- Tests: `tests/register.test.tsx` covering an ACTION item with and without a recommendation, and Accept all mixing both kinds.
response.title: session-decisions: an Accept button for ACTION items that carry a recommendation

response.body:
The plugins here are written for Claude Code. #118 (merged as #123) made the skills' scripts portable: each script now lives in its skill's own directory and SKILL.md calls it through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, so a skill installed by `npx skills add`, OpenCode's `skills` config or a plain skills folder can run it. That fixes the paths, nothing more. This issue is the rest: port what can be ported to other harnesses, starting with OpenCode, and give the plugins that need it a per-harness layer.

**What each plugin depends on today:**
- **forge-release, forge-tracker, worktree-tidy, term-recorder:** a skill plus standard-library Python. These should mostly work anywhere once the paths are right. Claude Code-only pieces:
  - the slash commands (`commands/*.md`);
  - worktree-tidy's session-start hook (`hooks/hooks.json`);
  - term-recorder's `allowed-tools` pre-approval;
  - forge-tracker's catchup/next/groom commands.
- **session-decisions:** a Claude Code function-hooks mod (pane, TaskCreate labelling, hand-off checks, `decision_*` tools) plus a skill. Only the skill and its no-plugin fallback (#114) work elsewhere.
- **session-history:** wraps the claude-session-index CLI, which reads Claude Code transcripts.

**To decide and build:**
1. **Survey:** for each plugin, list what works unchanged in OpenCode, what needs a per-harness equivalent (commands, hooks, tool pre-approval, MCP tools, a UI surface) and what can't port. Test with a real OpenCode install, not from docs alone.
2. **Layout for per-harness parts:** for example `plugins/<name>/harness/<harness>/` next to the shared skill and scripts, with the shared skill text written harness-neutral and each harness's extras (OpenCode plugin/commands, Claude Code hooks/commands) kept beside it. Record the convention in AGENTS.md, as was done for the minimum Claude Code version.
3. **OpenCode first:** port the skill-plus-script plugins and their commands. For session-decisions, decide whether an OpenCode plugin (its plugin API, a TUI or tool surface) can carry the queue, or whether the skill's labelled-list fallback is the OpenCode story.
4. **CI:** at least a smoke test that each portable skill's script runs from a skills-folder install, not only from the Claude Code plugin cache.
5. **Install docs** per harness in each README and the top-level README.

Related: #118 and #123 (paths), #114 (session-decisions' no-plugin fallback), #124 (minimum Claude Code version), lokkju/infra#214 (headless agents for the cattle runner, which may pick OpenCode).
response.title: Port the plugins to other harnesses (OpenCode first), with per-harness parts where a plugin needs them

response.body:
Part of #12 (forge-tracker). Builds on the forge read layer (#21), plus a small set of writes.

**`/groom`** keeps the tracker telling the truth, so that `/catchup` and `/next` rank real work. In practice the board drifts in predictable ways, and a ranking built on a drifted board ranks finished work as ready.

**The checks:**
- **Merged but still open:** an issue that a merged PR/MR references (`Closes #N`, `#N` in the title or branch) but that is still open. This is verified against the default branch, not taken on trust.
- **Labels disagreeing with milestones:** a tier label with no matching milestone, or a milestone whose tier label is missing.
- **A blocked label with nothing linked**, or links whose blocker is closed.
- **Decided but still waiting:** an issue labelled needs-a-human or decision that has a ruling comment after the label was added.
- **Stale branches:** remote branches with no open PR/MR whose commits are all on the default branch, so they are candidates to delete.
- **Stale or conflicted PRs/MRs:** open ones with merge conflicts, or no activity for N days.
- **Likely duplicates:** title and term similarity among open issues and those closed recently.
- **Placeholder due dates** shared by many issues, which skew any ordering by due date.

**Behaviour:**
- **Report first, read-only by default.** Every proposed change is listed with its evidence. Nothing is written until the user approves, item by item or as a batch.
- **Approved writes:** close with a resolution comment naming the PR/MR, fix labels or milestones, remove a blocked label, delete a merged branch. Each goes through forge-tracker's optional write-wrapper (#12), so a repo can enforce its own scrubbing or comment format.
- **Never acts on an inference it couldn't verify:** an "unclear" bucket is left for the user.
- **Output:** text and `--json`, with FAILED reads stated plainly, never as an empty section.
response.title: forge-tracker: /groom finds tracker drift (merged-but-open issues, label and milestone mismatches, stale branches) and fixes it on approval
